props.title: Lagot is loquat, not wood apple
props.leftBody: Evergreen subtropical tree. Soft yellow-orange fruit in clusters. Native to China. Eaten fresh in March and April.
props.rightBody: Hard woody shell. Brown aromatic pulp. Different genus. Different season. Different market.
props.foot: Confirm the Latin name before you pay for plants.

props.title: If the Latin name is wrong, stop

items.label: Loquat

items.sub: Aegle marmelos. Another lookalike in search.

props.title: A spreading evergreen, not a bush
props.foot: Plan canopy room now, not in year eight.

items.sub: Spreading crown. Needs a real grid, not a fence line of leftovers.

items.label: Evergreen
items.sub: Shade all year. Intercrops only work while the trees are young.

items.label: Cluster fruit
items.sub: One clip per bunch. Pulling fruit bruises and rots the lot.

items.label: Long life
items.sub: Peak yield around year fifteen. This is an orchard, not an annual.

props.title: Chinese fruit. Indian niche. No package.

items.sub: Scattered belts. You must build the market by hand.

props.title: Rose family. Evergreen. Not mango.

items.sub: Thinning, frame, bloom care, fruit in clusters.

items.label: Unlike apple
items.sub: Evergreen. Subtropical. Spring harvest in India.

items.label: Unlike mango
items.sub: Different pests, different season, different pack.

items.label: Unlike kaitha
items.sub: Soft fruit. No crowbar. No brown pulp.

props.title: Leaf first, fruit story second
props.foot: A felted leaf underside is a loquat tell.

items.label: Thick leaf
items.sub: Leathery. Not a thin citrus leaf.

items.label: Felt below
items.sub: Rusty hairs on the underside are common.

items.label: Not trifoliate
items.sub: If you see bael’s three leaflets, you are in the wrong queue.
